text.name: Caterpie

attacks.name: Flock
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Caterpie and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

text.flavor: Its short feet are tipped with suction pads that enable it to tirelessly climb slopes and walls.

text.name: Metapod

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Exoskeleton
abilities.text: This Pokémon takes 20 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

text.flavor: Even though it is encased in a sturdy shell, the body inside is tender. It can’t withstand a harsh attack.

text.name: Butterfree

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Tricolored Scales
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon during your turn, you may make your opponent's Active Pokémon Burned, Confused, and Poisoned.

text.flavor: It collects honey every day. It rubs honey onto the hairs on its legs to carry it back to its nest.

text.name: Shroomish
text.flavor: It spouts poison spores from the top of its head. These spores cause pain all over if inhaled.

text.name: Breloom

attacks.name: Impact Blow
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can’t use Impact Blow.

text.flavor: It scatters poisonous spores and throws powerful punches while its foe is hampered by inhaled spores.

attacks.name: Counter
attacks.text: If this Pokémon was damaged by an attack during your opponent's last turn, this attack does that much more damage.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

text.name: Pansage
text.flavor: It's good at finding berries and gathers them from all over. It's kind enough to share them with friends.

text.name: Simisage

attacks.name: Return
attacks.text: You may draw cards until you have 6 cards in your hand.

text.flavor: Ill tempered, it fights by swinging its barbed tail around wildly. The leaf growing on its head is very bitter.

text.name: Sewaddle

attacks.name: Grass Munch
attacks.text: Discard a {Grass} Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

text.flavor: Since this Pokémon makes its own clothes out of leaves, it is a popular mascot for fashion designers.

text.name: Swadloon

attacks.name: Trip Over
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

text.flavor: It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves. It stays on the move, eating leaves in forests.

text.name: Leavanny

attacks.name: Healing Circle
attacks.text: Heal all damage from each of your Benched Pokémon. If you healed any damage in this way, shuffle this Pokémon and all attached cards into your deck.

text.flavor: It keeps its eggs warm with heat from fermenting leaves. It also uses leaves to make warm wrappings for Sewaddle.

text.name: Maractus

attacks.name: Ditch and Shake
attacks.text: Discard any number of Pokémon Tool cards from your hand. This attack does 50 damage for each card you discarded in this way.

text.flavor: Once each year, this Pokémon scatters its seeds. They're jam-packed with nutrients, making them a precious food source out in the desert.

text.name: Shelmet
text.flavor: It has a strange physiology that responds to electricity. When together with Karrablast, Shelmet evolves for some reason.

text.name: Accelgor

attacks.name: Ninja Tornado
attacks.text: If this Pokémon moved from your Bench to the Active Spot this turn, this attack can be used for {Grass}.

text.flavor: Discarding its shell made it nimble. To keep itself from dehydrating, it wraps its body in bands of membrane.

text.name: Virizion

attacks.name: Bail Out
attacks.text: Put up to 2 Pokémon from your discard pile into your hand.

text.flavor: Legends say this Pokémon confounded opponents with its swift movements.

text.name: Phantump
text.flavor: With a voice like a human child's, it cries out to lure adults deep into the forest, getting them lost among the trees.

text.name: Trevenant
text.flavor: Small roots that extend from the tips of this Pokémon's feet can tie into the trees of the forest and give Trevenant control over them.

text.name: Grubbin

attacks.name: Energize
attacks.text: Attach a {Lightning} Energy card from your discard pile to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Surprise Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

text.flavor: It uses its big jaws to dig nests into the forest floor, and it loves to feed on sweet tree sap.

text.name: Dewpider
text.flavor: Dewpider normally lives underwater. When it comes onto land in search of food, it takes water with it in the form of a bubble on its head.

text.name: Araquanid

attacks.name: Bubble Launch
attacks.text: Move an Energy from this Pokémon to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

text.flavor: It acts as a caretaker for Dewpider, putting them inside its bubble and letting them eat any leftover food.

attacks.name: Queen's Orders
attacks.text: You may discard any number of your Benched Pokémon. This attack does 40 more damage for each Benched Pokémon you discarded in this way.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Drain Punch
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: G-Max Drum Solo
attacks.text: This attack also does 40 damage to 2 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

rules.label: VMAX rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

text.name: Gossifleur
text.flavor: It whirls around in the wind while singing a joyous song. This delightful display has charmed many into raising this Pokémon.

text.name: Eldegoss

attacks.name: Sunny Wind
attacks.text: Heal 20 damage from this Pokémon.

text.flavor: The cotton on the head of this Pokémon can be spun into a glossy, gorgeous yarn—a Galar regional specialty.

attacks.name: Sweet Impact
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

text.name: Zarude

attacks.name: Wild Whip
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 more damage.

text.flavor: Once the vines on Zarude's body tear off, they become nutrients in the soil. This helps the plants of the forest grow.

text.name: Vulpix
text.flavor: As each tail grows, its fur becomes more lustrous. When held, it feels slightly warm.

text.name: Vulpix
text.flavor: As each tail grows, its fur becomes more lustrous. When held, it feels slightly warm.

text.name: Ninetales
text.flavor: Very smart and very vengeful. Grabbing one of its many tails could result in a 1,000-year curse.

text.name: Ninetales

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Byway of the Nine-Tailed Fox
abilities.text: The Retreat Cost of each of your Pokémon that has any {Fire} Energy attached is {Colorless}{Colorless} less.

text.flavor: Very smart and very vengeful. Grabbing one of its many tails could result in a 1,000-year curse.

text.name: Growlithe

attacks.name: Warm Up
attacks.text: Search your deck for a {Fire} Energy card and attach it to 1 of your Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

text.flavor: Extremely loyal, it will fearlessly bark at any opponent to protect its own Trainer from harm.

text.name: Arcanine

attacks.name: Heat Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

text.flavor: A Pokémon that has long been admired for its beauty. It runs agilely as if on wings.

text.name: Slugma
text.flavor: Its body is made of magma. If it doesn't keep moving, its body will cool and harden.

text.name: Magcargo

attacks.name: Body Splash
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. For each tails, discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

text.flavor: Its body is as hot as lava and is always billowing. Flames will occasionally burst from its shell.

text.name: Victini

attacks.name: Fiery Cheering
attacks.text: Attach a basic Energy card from your discard pile to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

text.flavor: When it shares the infinite energy it creates, that being's entire body will be overflowing with power.

text.name: Pansear

attacks.name: Surprise Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

text.flavor: This Pokémon lives in caves in volcanoes. The fire within the tuft on its head can reach 600 degrees Fahrenheit.

text.name: Simisear

attacks.name: Fling Fire
attacks.text: Discard up to 2 basic Energy cards from your hand. This attack does 60 damage for each card you discarded in this way.

text.flavor: When it gets excited, embers rise from its head and tail and it gets hot. For some reason, it loves sweets.

attacks.name: Confuse Ray
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Poltergeist
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand. This attack does 40 damage for each Trainer card you find there.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Cursed Shimmer
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, your opponent can't play any Pokémon Tool cards from their hand.

attacks.name: Max Poltergeist
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand. This attack does 70 damage for each Trainer card you find there.

rules.label: VMAX rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

text.name: Heatmor

attacks.name: Flame Cloak
attacks.text: Attach a {Fire} Energy card from your discard pile to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Exciting Flame
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has at least 3 extra Energy attached (in addition to this attack's cost), this attack also does 180 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

text.flavor: A flame serves as its tongue, melting through the hard shell of Durant so that Heatmor can devour their insides.

text.name: Oricorio

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Lesson in Zeal
abilities.text: All of your Fusion Strike Pokémon take 20 less damage from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon (after applying Weakness and Resistance). You can't apply more than 1 Lesson in Zeal Ability at a time.

attacks.name: Glistening Droplets
attacks.text: Put 5 damage counters on your opponent's Pokémon in any way you like.

text.flavor: This Oricorio has drunk red nectar. If its Trainer gives the wrong order, this passionate Pokémon becomes fiercely angry.

attacks.name: Blaze Kick
attacks.text: Discard 2 {Fire} Energy from this Pokémon.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: All-Out Shot
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: G-Max Fireball
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned. During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

rules.label: VMAX rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

text.name: Sizzlipede
text.flavor: It wraps prey up with its heated body, cooking them in its coils. Once they're well-done, it will voraciously nibble them down to the last morsel.

text.name: Sizzlipede

attacks.name: Singe
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

text.flavor: It wraps prey up with its heated body, cooking them in its coils. Once they're well-done, it will voraciously nibble them down to the last morsel.

text.name: Centiskorch

attacks.name: Coil
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon's attacks do 90 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

text.flavor: While its burning body is already dangerous on its own, this excessively hostile Pokémon also has large and very sharp fangs.

text.name: Centiskorch
text.flavor: While its burning body is already dangerous on its own, this excessively hostile Pokémon also has large and very sharp fangs.

text.name: Shellder
text.flavor: Its hard shell repels any kind of attack. It is vulnerable only when its shell is open.

text.name: Cloyster

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Shell Armor
abilities.text: This Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Aqua Split
attacks.text: This attack also does 30 damage to 2 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

text.flavor: Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.

text.name: Staryu

attacks.name: Soak in Water
attacks.text: Attach a {Water} Energy card from your hand to this Pokémon.

text.flavor: No number of injuries can bother Staryu. Its amazing regenerative powers return it to its previous state in half a day!

text.name: Starmie

attacks.name: Multishot Star
attacks.text: Discard any amount of {Water} Energy from this Pokémon. Then, for each Energy card you discarded in this way, choose 1 of your opponent's Pokémon and do 30 damage to it. (You can choose the same Pokémon more than once.) This damage isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance.

text.flavor: It rotates its geometrically shaped body to swim through the water. It always seems to be sending out mysterious radio waves.

text.name: Lapras

attacks.name: Icy Wind
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Splash Arch
attacks.text: Put all Energy attached to this Pokémon into your hand. This attack does 100 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

text.flavor: Crossing icy seas is no issue for this cold-resistant Pokémon. Its smooth skin is a little cool to the touch.

text.name: Totodile
text.flavor: Its powerful, well-developed jaws are capable of crushing anything. Even its Trainer must be careful.

text.name: Croconaw
text.flavor: Once it bites down, it won't let go until it loses its fangs. New fangs quickly grow into place.

text.name: Feraligatr

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Rowdy
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon during your turn, you must flip a coin. If heads, discard the top 5 cards of your opponent's deck. If tails, discard the top 5 cards of your deck.

attacks.name: Crunch
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

text.flavor: When it bites with its massive and powerful jaws, it shakes its head and savagely tears its victim up.

text.name: Marill

attacks.name: Aqua Liner
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Let's All Rollout
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each of your Benched Pokémon that has the Let's All Rollout attack.

text.flavor: Even after Marill swims in a cold sea, its water-repellent fur dries almost as soon as Marill leaves the water. That's why this Pokémon is never cold.

text.name: Azumarill

attacks.name: Dive and Rescue
attacks.text: Put up to 3 in any combination of Pokémon and Supporter cards from your discard pile into your hand.

text.flavor: The bubble-like pattern on its stomach helps it camouflage itself when it's in the water.

text.name: Qwilfish

attacks.name: Collect
attacks.text: Draw a card.

text.flavor: The small spikes covering its body developed from scales. They inject a toxin that causes fainting.

text.name: Mantine

attacks.name: Bounce
attacks.text: You may switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

text.flavor: As it majestically swims, it doesn't care if Remoraid attach to it to scavenge for its leftovers.

text.name: Mudkip
text.flavor: To alert it, the fin on its head senses the flow of water. It has the strength to heft boulders.

text.name: Marshtomp

attacks.name: Energy Loop
attacks.text: Put an Energy attached to this Pokémon into your hand.

text.flavor: Living on muddy ground that provides poor footing has made its legs sturdy.

text.name: Swampert

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Muddy Maker
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may attach a {Water} Energy card or a {Fighting} Energy card from your hand to 1 of your Pokémon.

attacks.name: Earthquake
attacks.text: This attack also does 20 damage to each of your Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

text.flavor: It can swim while towing a large ship. It bashes down foes with a swing of its thick arms.

text.name: Clamperl
text.flavor: Clamperl's pearls are exceedingly precious. They can be more than 10 times as costly as Shellder's pearls.

text.name: Huntail

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Single Strike Jammer
abilities.text: Your opponent's Single Strike Pokémon's attacks cost {Colorless} more.

text.flavor: Deep seas are their habitat. According to tradition, when Huntail wash up onshore, something unfortunate will happen.

text.name: Gorebyss

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Rapid Strike Canceler
abilities.text: Your opponent's Rapid Strike Pokémon in play have no Abilities.

attacks.name: Draining Kiss
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

text.flavor: It sucks bodily fluids out of its prey. The leftover meat sinks to the seafloor, where it becomes food for other Pokémon.

text.name: Panpour

attacks.name: Pry
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand.

text.flavor: The water stored inside the tuft on its head is full of nutrients. Plants that receive its water grow large.

text.name: Simipour

attacks.name: Water Pulse
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Circus Soaking
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand. This attack does 60 damage for each Supporter card you find there.

text.flavor: It prefers places with clean water. When its tuft runs low, it replenishes it by siphoning up water with its tail.

text.name: Basculin

attacks.name: Swarm the Wound
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each damage counter on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

text.flavor: Known for their violence, these Pokémon have the most fights with schools of red-striped Basculin.

text.name: Galarian Darumaka

attacks.name: Reckless Charge
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this Pokémon also does 10 damage to itself.

text.flavor: The colder they get, the more energetic they are. They freeze their breath to make snowballs, using them as ammo for playful snowball fights.

text.name: Galarian Darmanitan

attacks.name: Powder Snow
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Daruma Headbutt
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has any damage counters on it, this attack can be used for {Water}.

text.flavor: Though it has a gentle disposition, it's also very strong. It will quickly freeze the snowball on its head before going for a headbutt.

attacks.name: Dancing Shuriken
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 80 damage for each heads.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

text.name: Clauncher
text.flavor: It moves around by jetting water from its right pincer. It has a poor sense of balance, so it's terrible at swimming straight.

text.name: Clawitzer

attacks.name: Snipe Shot
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

text.flavor: Its right arm is packed with meat. When its pincer falls off, it's exported to be used as a cooking ingredient.

attacks.name: Trigger Avalanche
attacks.text: Discard the top 2 cards of your opponent's deck.

attacks.name: Destroyer Punch
attacks.text: This attack does 60 more damage for each damage counter on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

text.name: Pyukumuku

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Pitch a Pyukumuku
abilities.text: Once during your turn, if this Pokémon is in your hand, you may reveal it and put it on the bottom of your deck. If you do, draw a card. You can't use more than 1 Pitch a Pyukumuku Ability each turn.

text.flavor: It's covered in a slime that keeps its skin moist, allowing it to stay on land for days without drying up.

attacks.name: Aqua Bullet
attacks.text: This attack also does 20 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Double Gunner
abilities.text: You must discard a {Water} Energy card from your hand in order to use this Ability. Once during your turn, you may choose 2 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon and put 2 damage counters on each of them.

attacks.name: G-Max Spiral
attacks.text: You may put an Energy attached to this Pokémon into your hand. If you do, this attack does 70 more damage.

rules.label: VMAX rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

text.name: Chewtle
text.flavor: It starts off battles by attacking with its rock-hard horn, but as soon as the opponent flinches, this Pokémon bites down and never lets go.

text.name: Drednaw

attacks.name: Hard Bite
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 50 more damage.

text.flavor: This Pokémon rapidly extends its retractable neck to sink its sharp fangs into distant enemies and take them down.

text.name: Arrokuda
text.flavor: After it's eaten its fill, its movements become extremely sluggish. That's when Cramorant swallows it up.

text.name: Barraskewda
text.flavor: It spins its tail fins to propel itself, surging forward at speeds of over 100 knots before ramming prey and spearing into them.

text.name: Snom

attacks.name: Find Ice
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 {Water} Energy cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

text.flavor: It eats snow that piles up on the ground. The more snow it eats, the bigger and more impressive the spikes on its back grow.

text.name: Frosmoth

attacks.name: Icy Wind
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Blizzard Loop
attacks.text: Put all Energy attached to this Pokémon into your hand.

text.flavor: It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

text.name: Voltorb

attacks.name: Single Shot Blast
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

text.flavor: Usually found in power plants. Easily mistaken for a Poké Ball, it has zapped many people.

text.name: Electrode

attacks.name: Sonic Boom
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance.

attacks.name: Explosion
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 90 damage to itself.

text.flavor: It stores an overflowing amount of electric energy inside its body. Even a small shock makes it explode.

text.name: Plusle

attacks.name: Spark Duo
attacks.text: If 1 of your Minun used an attack during your last turn, this attack does 100 more damage.

text.flavor: It absorbs electricity from telephone poles. It shorts out its body to create crackling noises.

text.name: Minun

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

text.flavor: It cheers on friends. If its friends are losing, its body lets off more and more sparks.

text.name: Shinx
text.flavor: All of its fur dazzles if danger is sensed. It flees while the foe is momentarily blinded.

text.name: Luxio
text.flavor: Strong electricity courses through the tips of its sharp claws. A light scratch causes fainting in foes.

text.name: Luxray
text.flavor: Luxray's ability to see through objects comes in handy when it's scouting for danger.

text.name: Rotom

attacks.name: Surprise Short
attacks.text: Discard all Pokémon Tools from all of your opponent's Pokémon.

text.flavor: With a body made of plasma, it can inhabit all sorts of machines. It loves to surprise others.

text.name: Tynamo

attacks.name: Thunder Wave
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

text.flavor: One alone can emit only a trickle of electricity, so a group of them gathers to unleash a powerful electric shock.

text.name: Eelektrik

attacks.name: Thunder
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 20 damage to itself.

text.flavor: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

text.name: Eelektross

attacks.name: Upper Shock
attacks.text: If this Pokémon evolved from Eelektrik during this turn, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Wild Charge
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

text.flavor: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

text.name: Helioptile
text.flavor: The sun powers this Pokémon's electricity generation. Interruption of that process stresses Helioptile to the point of weakness.

text.name: Heliolisk

attacks.name: Electrobullet
attacks.text: This attack also does 20 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

text.flavor: One Heliolisk basking in the sun with its frill outspread is all it would take to produce enough electricity to power a city.

text.name: Charjabug
text.flavor: Its digestive processes convert the leaves it eats into electricity. An electric sac in its belly stores the electricity for later use.

text.name: Vikavolt

attacks.name: Electro Blaster
attacks.text: Discard 2 {Lightning} Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 200 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

text.flavor: If it carries a Charjabug to use as a spare battery, a flying Vikavolt can rapidly fire high-powered beams of electricity.

text.name: Zeraora

attacks.name: Wild Charge
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 20 damage to itself.

text.flavor: It approaches its enemies at the speed of lightning, then tears them limb from limb with its sharp claws.

attacks.name: Smash Turn
attacks.text: You may switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Electrobullet
attacks.text: This attack also does 30 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Bolt Storm
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each {Lightning} Energy attached to all of your Pokémon.

attacks.name: Max Bolt
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use Max Bolt.

rules.label: VMAX rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

text.name: Toxel
text.flavor: It manipulates the chemical makeup of its poison to produce electricity. The voltage is weak, but it can cause a tingling paralysis.

text.name: Toxel

attacks.name: Growl
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon's attacks do 30 less damage (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

text.flavor: It manipulates the chemical makeup of its poison to produce electricity. The voltage is weak, but it can cause a tingling paralysis.

text.name: Toxtricity

attacks.name: Punk Shock
attacks.text: You may choose to make your opponent's Active Pokémon Paralyzed. If you do, this Pokémon also does 70 damage to itself.

text.flavor: This short-tempered and aggressive Pokémon chugs stagnant water to absorb any toxins it might contain.

text.name: Toxtricity

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Maximum Downer
abilities.text: If all your Pokémon in play are Fusion Strike Pokémon, your opponent's Pokémon VMAX in play get -30 HP.

text.flavor: It has an electrical organ on its chest. While generating electricity, it fills its surroundings with what sounds like the strumming of a bass guitar.

text.name: Morpeko

attacks.name: Targeted Spark
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

text.flavor: It carries electrically roasted seeds with it as if they're precious treasures. No matter how much it eats, it always gets hungry again in short order.

text.name: Jigglypuff

attacks.name: Let's All Rollout
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each of your Benched Pokémon that has the Let's All Rollout attack.

text.flavor: The songs they sing are totally different depending on the region they live in. Some even sound like they're shouting!

text.name: Wigglytuff

attacks.name: Find Treasure
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 cards and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

text.flavor: When it gets angry, it inhales with all its might, and its body gradually inflates. Sometimes they can grow 20 times larger!

text.name: Jynx

attacks.name: Double Draw
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

attacks.name: Dazzle Dance
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

text.flavor: Its strange cries sound like human language. There are some musicians who compose songs for Jynx to sing.

attacks.name: Energy Mix
attacks.text: Search your deck for an Energy card and attach it to 1 of your Fusion Strike Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Psychic Leap
attacks.text: You may shuffle this Pokémon and all attached cards into your deck.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Cross Fusion Strike
attacks.text: Choose 1 of your Benched Fusion Strike Pokémon's attacks and use it as this attack.

attacks.name: Max Miracle
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

rules.label: VMAX rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

text.name: Snubbull
text.flavor: In contrast to its appearance, it's quite timid. When playing with other puppy Pokémon, it sometimes gets bullied.

text.name: Granbull

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Dig Up
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon during your turn, you may put up to 2 Pokémon Tool cards from your discard pile into your hand.

text.flavor: Although it's popular with young people, Granbull is timid and sensitive, so it's totally incompetent as a watchdog.

text.name: Galarian Corsola
text.flavor: Sudden climate change wiped out this ancient kind of Corsola. This Pokémon absorbs others' life-force through its branches.

text.name: Galarian Cursola

attacks.name: Force Regeneration
attacks.text: Put a Basic Pokémon V from your opponent's discard pile onto their Bench. If you do, put damage counters on that Pokémon until its remaining HP is 30.

text.flavor: Be cautious of the ectoplasmic body surrounding its soul. You'll become stiff as stone if you touch it.

text.name: Mawile

attacks.name: Chomp Chomp Hold
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon's attacks cost {Colorless} more, and its Retreat Cost is {Colorless} more.

text.flavor: It chomps with its gaping mouth. Its huge jaws are actually steel horns that have been transformed.

text.name: Deoxys

attacks.name: Photon Boost
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has any Fusion Strike Energy attached, this attack does 80 more damage.

text.flavor: DNA from a space virus mutated and became a Pokémon. It appears where auroras are seen.

text.name: Munna
text.flavor: It eats dreams and releases mist. The mist is pink when it's eating a good dream, and black when it's eating a nightmare.

text.name: Musharna

attacks.name: Sleep Inducer
attacks.text: Switch 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon with their Active Pokémon. The new Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Psychic
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

text.flavor: It drowses and dreams all the time. It's best to leave it be if it's just woken up, as it's a terrible grump when freshly roused from sleep.

text.name: Sigilyph

attacks.name: Joust
attacks.text: Before doing damage, discard all Pokémon Tools from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Reflect Energy
attacks.text: Move an Energy from this Pokémon to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

text.flavor: A discovery was made in the desert where Sigilyph fly. The ruins of what may have been an ancient city were found beneath the sands.

text.name: Meloetta

attacks.name: Melodious Echo
attacks.text: This attack does 70 damage for each Fusion Strike Energy attached to all of your Pokémon.

text.flavor: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.

text.name: Sandygast
text.flavor: If you build sand mounds when you're playing, destroy them before you go home, or they may get possessed and become Sandygast.

text.name: Palossand

attacks.name: Oppressing Sandstorm
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Basic Pokémon, it is Knocked Out.

text.flavor: Once it has whipped up a sandstorm to halt its opponents in their tracks, this terrifying Pokémon snatches away their vitality.

text.name: Indeedee

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

text.flavor: They diligently serve people and Pokémon so they can gather feelings of gratitude. The females are particularly good at babysitting.

text.name: Dreepy

attacks.name: Infestation
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

text.flavor: If this weak Pokémon is by itself, a mere child could defeat it. But if Dreepy has friends to help it train, it can evolve and become much stronger.

text.name: Drakloak

attacks.name: U-turn
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

text.flavor: Without a Dreepy to place on its head and care for, it gets so uneasy it'll try to substitute any Pokémon it finds for the missing Dreepy.

text.name: Dragapult

attacks.name: Fusion Strike Assault
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage for each of your Fusion Strike Pokémon in play.

text.flavor: Apparently the Dreepy inside Dragapult's horns eagerly look forward to being launched out at Mach speeds.

text.name: Sandshrew

attacks.name: Dig It Up
attacks.text: Look at the top card of your deck. You may discard that card.

attacks.name: Let's All Rollout
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each of your Benched Pokémon that has the Let's All Rollout attack.

text.flavor: When its skin gets wrinkled from moisture, it heads for a volcano. It lies flat on a spot with a lot of geothermal heat and dries itself out.

text.name: Sandslash

attacks.name: Dig Uppercut
attacks.text: Put a card from your discard pile into your hand.

text.flavor: Thanks to its thick claws, it's good at climbing trees. There are plenty of Sandslash that park themselves in trees and go right to sleep.

text.name: Mankey
text.flavor: If one gets angry, all the others around it will get angry, so silence is a rare visitor in a troop of Mankey.

text.name: Primeape

attacks.name: Gut Punch
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Pokémon V, this attack does 60 more damage.

text.flavor: The blood vessels in its brain are sturdier than those of other Pokémon, so it can stay healthy despite its constant raging.

text.name: Geodude
text.flavor: It uses both hands to climb precipitous cliffs. People who see it in action have been known to take up bouldering.

text.name: Graveler
text.flavor: It travels by rolling down cliffs. If it falls into a river, it will explode with its last gasp.

text.name: Golem

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Desperate Blast
abilities.text: If this Pokémon is in the Active Spot and is Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon, put 10 damage counters on the Attacking Pokémon.

attacks.name: Double-Edge
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

text.flavor: It detonates its own body. The power from that explosion can propel it up steep mountain paths with amazing speed.

text.name: Onix

attacks.name: Guard Press
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

text.flavor: It rapidly bores through the ground at 50 mph by squirming and twisting its massive, rugged body.

text.name: Steelix

attacks.name: Powerful Rage
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Earthquake
attacks.text: This attack also does 30 damage to each of your Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

text.flavor: It is thought its body transformed as a result of iron accumulating internally from swallowing soil.

text.name: Gligar

attacks.name: Poison Sting
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

text.flavor: It flies straight at its target's face, then clamps down on the startled victim to inject poison.

text.name: Gliscor

attacks.name: Cut Down
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Venomous Hit
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

text.flavor: Its flight is soundless. It uses its lengthy tail to carry off its prey... Then its elongated fangs do the rest.

text.name: Makuhita
text.flavor: There's a rumor of a traditional recipe for stew that Trainers can use to raise strong Makuhita.

text.name: Hariyama

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Guts
abilities.text: If this Pokémon would be Knocked Out by damage from an attack, flip a coin. If heads, this Pokémon is not Knocked Out, and its remaining HP becomes 10.

text.flavor: Hariyama that are big and fat aren't necessarily strong. There are some small ones that move nimbly and use moves skillfully.

text.name: Baltoy
text.flavor: It was discovered in ancient ruins. While moving, it constantly spins. It stands on one foot even when asleep.

text.name: Claydol

attacks.name: Rapid Spin
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon. If you do, your opponent switches their Active Pokémon with 1 of their Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Ancient Imprint
attacks.text: Put damage counters on your opponent's Active Pokémon until its remaining HP is 60.

text.flavor: It appears to have been born from clay dolls made by ancient people. It uses telekinesis to float and move.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

text.name: Drilbur
text.flavor: It's a digger, using its claws to burrow through the ground. It causes damage to vegetable crops, so many farmers have little love for it.

text.name: Landorus

attacks.name: Strafe
attacks.text: You may switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Earthen Boom
attacks.text: Move all Energy from this Pokémon to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like.

text.flavor: From the forces of lightning and wind, it creates energy to give nutrients to the soil and make the land abundant.

text.name: Pancham

attacks.name: Raised Bad
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 {Darkness} Energy cards and attach them to this Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

text.flavor: Wanting to make sure it's taken seriously, Pancham's always giving others a glare. But if it's not focusing, it ends up smiling.

text.name: Stufful
text.flavor: The way it protects itself by flailing its arms may be an adorable sight, but stay well away. This is flailing that can snap thick tree trunks.

text.name: Bewear

attacks.name: Split Spiral Punch
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

text.flavor: The moves it uses to take down its prey would make a martial artist jealous. It tucks subdued prey under its arms to carry them to its nest.

text.name: Clobbopus
text.flavor: Its tentacles tear off easily, but it isn't alarmed when that happens—it knows they'll grow back. It's about as smart as a three-year-old.

text.name: Grapploct
text.flavor: Searching for an opponent to test its skills against, it emerges onto land. Once the battle is over, it returns to the sea.

text.name: Falinks

attacks.name: Cliff Edge Formation
attacks.text: If your opponent has exactly 1 Prize card remaining, this attack does 160 more damage.

text.flavor: The six of them work together as one Pokémon. Teamwork is also their battle strategy, and they constantly change their formation as they fight.

text.name: Falinks
text.flavor: The six of them work together as one Pokémon. Teamwork is also their battle strategy, and they constantly change their formation as they fight.

attacks.name: Dark Slumber
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Pain Explosion
attacks.text: Put 3 damage counters on this Pokémon.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Fear and Panic
attacks.text: This attack does 60 damage for each of your opponent's Pokémon V and Pokémon-GX in play.

attacks.name: G-Max Swallow Up
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

rules.label: VMAX rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

text.name: Galarian Zigzagoon

attacks.name: Lick
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

text.flavor: Thought to be the oldest form of Zigzagoon, it moves in zigzags and wreaks havoc upon its surroundings.

text.name: Galarian Linoone
text.flavor: This very aggressive Pokémon will recklessly challenge opponents stronger than itself.

text.name: Galarian Obstagoon

attacks.name: Silence
attacks.text: Choose 1 of your opponent's Active Pokémon's attacks. During your opponent's next turn, that Pokémon can't use that attack.

attacks.name: Merciless Strike
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon already has any damage counters on it, this attack does 90 more damage.

text.flavor: It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.

text.name: Carvanha
text.flavor: With its sturdy jaws and fangs, it can easily chomp wooden boats to splinters. It fights with Basculin over food.

text.name: Sharpedo
text.flavor: It drinks in seawater and jets it from its rear to propel itself. It's very sensitive to the scent of blood.

text.name: Absol

attacks.name: Drag Off
attacks.text: Switch 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon with their Active Pokémon. This attack does 30 damage to the new Active Pokémon.

text.flavor: The elderly call it the disaster Pokémon and detest it, but interest in its power to predict disasters is on the rise.

text.name: Croagunk
text.flavor: Once diluted, its poison becomes medicinal. This Pokémon came into popularity after a pharmaceutical company chose it as a mascot.

text.name: Toxicroak

attacks.name: Severe Poison
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned. During Pokémon Checkup, put 4 damage counters on that Pokémon instead of 1.

text.flavor: It booms out a victory croak when its prey goes down in defeat. This Pokémon and Seismitoad are related species.

text.name: Darkrai
text.flavor: It can lull people to sleep and make them dream. It is active during nights of the new moon.

text.name: Trubbish

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Super Poison Breath
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

text.flavor: This Pokémon was born from a bag stuffed with trash. Galarian Weezing relish the fumes belched by Trubbish.

text.name: Garbodor

attacks.name: Poison Gas
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

text.flavor: The toxic liquid it launches from its right arm is so virulent that it can kill a weakened creature instantly.

text.name: Zorua
text.flavor: If a normally talkative child suddenly stops talking, it may have been replaced by Zorua.

text.name: Zoroark

attacks.name: Double Claw
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 40 damage for each heads.

text.flavor: If it thinks humans are going to discover its den, Zoroark shows them visions that make them wander around in the woods.

text.name: Vullaby

attacks.name: Air Slash
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

text.flavor: Vullaby grow quickly. Bones that have gotten too small for older Vullaby to wear often get passed down to younger ones in the nest.

text.name: Mandibuzz

attacks.name: Bone Block
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, Pokémon can't be played from your opponent's hand to evolve the Defending Pokémon.

text.flavor: They adorn themselves with bones. There seem to be fashion trends among them, as different bones come into and fall out of popularity.

text.name: Pangoro

attacks.name: Knocking Hammer
attacks.text: Discard the top card of your opponent's deck.

attacks.name: Shakedown
attacks.text: Discard a random card from your opponent's hand.

text.flavor: Using its leaf, Pangoro can predict the moves of its opponents. It strikes with punches that can turn a dump truck into scrap with just one hit.

text.name: Yveltal
text.flavor: When its life comes to an end, it absorbs the life energy of every living thing and turns into a cocoon once more.

text.name: Impidimp

attacks.name: Play Rough
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 more damage.

text.flavor: It sneaks into people's homes, stealing things and feasting on the negative energy of the frustrated occupants.

text.name: Morgrem

attacks.name: Crushing Blow
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

text.flavor: With sly cunning, it tries to lure people into the woods. Some believe it to have the power to make crops grow.

text.name: Grimmsnarl

attacks.name: Rear Attack
attacks.text: If you have 2 or fewer Benched Pokémon, this attack does 140 more damage.

text.flavor: Its hairs work like muscle fibers. When its hairs unfurl, they latch on to opponents, ensnaring them as tentacles would.

text.name: Morpeko

attacks.name: Explosive Discontent
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

text.flavor: Hunger hormones affect its temperament. Until its hunger is appeased, it gets up to all manner of evil deeds.

text.name: Galarian Meowth

attacks.name: Growl
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon's attacks do 20 less damage (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

text.flavor: These daring Pokémon have coins on their foreheads. Darker coins are harder, and harder coins garner more respect among Meowth.

text.name: Galarian Perrserker

attacks.name: Call to Muster
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 basic Energy cards and attach them to your Pokémon in any way you like. Then, shuffle your deck.

text.flavor: After many battles, it evolved dangerous claws that come together to form daggers when extended.

text.name: Skarmory

attacks.name: Steel Wing
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

text.flavor: Its body is draped in steel armor. It looks heavy, but it can fly at speeds of up to 185 miles an hour!

text.name: Excadrill

attacks.name: Rock Tomb
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

text.flavor: Known as the Drill King, this Pokémon can tunnel through the terrain at speeds of over 90 mph.

text.name: Durant

attacks.name: Adversity Jaws
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a {Fire} Pokémon, it is now Paralyzed.

text.flavor: With their large mandibles, these Pokémon can crunch their way through rock. They work together to protect their eggs from Sandaconda.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Fusion Strike System
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may draw cards until you have as many cards in your hand as you have Fusion Strike Pokémon in play.

attacks.name: Techno Blast
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

text.name: Klefki

attacks.name: Unlock
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

text.flavor: Long ago it lived in mines, but once the minerals that make up its diet became scarcer, Klefki began appearing in human settlements.

text.name: Togedemaru

attacks.name: Let's All Rollout
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each of your Benched Pokémon that has the Let's All Rollout attack.

text.flavor: When it's in trouble, it curls up into a ball, makes its fur spikes stand on end, and then discharges electricity indiscriminately.

text.name: Meltan

attacks.name: Iron Intake
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

text.flavor: It melts particles of iron and other metals found in the subsoil, so it can absorb them into its body of molten steel.

text.name: Melmetal

attacks.name: Ingot Swing
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks from Pokémon that have an Ability.

attacks.name: Blasting Hammer
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

text.flavor: Revered long ago for its capacity to create iron from nothing, for some reason it has come back to life after 3,000 years.

text.name: Corviknight

attacks.name: Steel Wing
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Power Cyclone
attacks.text: Move an Energy from this Pokémon to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

text.flavor: With their great intellect and flying skills, these Pokémon very successfully act as the Galar region's airborne taxi service.

text.name: Cufant

attacks.name: High Horsepower
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 20 damage to itself.

text.flavor: If a job requires serious strength, this Pokémon will excel at it. Its copper body tarnishes in the rain, turning a vibrant green color.

text.name: Copperajah

attacks.name: High Horsepower
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

text.flavor: These Pokémon live in herds. Their trunks have incredible grip strength, strong enough to crush giant rocks into powder.

text.name: Latias

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Red Assist
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may attach a {Psychic} Energy card from your hand to 1 of your Latios.

attacks.name: Dyna Barrier
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks from Pokémon VMAX.

text.flavor: It can telepathically communicate with people. It changes its appearance using its down that refracts light.

text.name: Latios

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Blue Assist
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may attach a {Psychic} Energy card from your hand to 1 of your Latias.

attacks.name: Luster Purge
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon.

text.flavor: It understands human speech and is highly intelligent. It is a tender Pokémon that dislikes fighting.

text.name: Goomy
text.flavor: Their horns are powerful sensors. As soon as Goomy pick up any sign of enemies, they go into hiding. This is how they've survived.

text.name: Sliggoo

attacks.name: Body Slam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

text.flavor: The lump on its back contains its tiny brain. It thinks only of food and escaping its enemies.

text.name: Goodra

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Slimy Room
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, whenever your opponent tries to attach an Energy card from their hand to a Pokémon, they must flip a coin. If tails, your opponent discards that Energy card instead of attaching it, and this doesn't use up their Energy attachment for the turn.

text.flavor: Its form of offense is forcefully stretching out its horns. The strikes land 100 times harder than any blow from a heavyweight boxer.

text.name: Turtonator

attacks.name: Shell Trap
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, if this Pokémon is damaged by an attack (even if it is Knocked Out), put 8 damage counters on the Attacking Pokémon.

text.flavor: Eating sulfur in its volcanic habitat is what causes explosive compounds to develop in its shell. Its droppings are also dangerously explosive.

text.name: Meowth

attacks.name: Pay Day
attacks.text: Draw a card.

text.flavor: It washes its face regularly to keep the coin on its forehead spotless. It doesn't get along with Galarian Meowth.

text.name: Persian

attacks.name: Pay Day
attacks.text: Draw a card.

text.flavor: Its elegant and refined behavior clashes with that of the barbaric Perrserker. The relationship between the two is one of mutual disdain.

attacks.name: No Reprieve
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon's attacks do 80 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Rampage Drill
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

rules.label: V rule
rules.text: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

text.name: Chansey

attacks.name: Drain Slap
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

text.flavor: Because the eggs on their bellies have been overharvested by people in the past, the Chansey population remains very small.

text.name: Blissey

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Expert in Roundness
abilities.text: Prevent all damage done to each of your Pokémon that has the Let's All Rollout attack by attacks from your opponent's Pokémon VMAX.

attacks.name: Let's All Rollout
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each of your Benched Pokémon that has the Let's All Rollout attack.

text.flavor: This Pokémon is overflowing with love. Only Chansey that share a strong bond with their Trainer can evolve, so people say.

text.name: Kangaskhan

attacks.name: Coordinated One-Two Punch
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 100 more damage.

text.flavor: You shouldn't get close to the child when it's playing outside its mother's pouch. Its mother is always nearby watching over it.

text.name: Eevee

attacks.name: Continuous Steps
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. This attack does 30 damage for each heads.

text.flavor: Thanks to its unstable genetic makeup, this special Pokémon conceals many different possible evolutions.

text.name: Snorlax
text.flavor: This Pokémon's stomach is so strong, even eating moldy or rotten food will not affect it.

text.name: Dunsparce

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.name: Mysterious Nest
abilities.text: {Colorless} Pokémon in play (both yours and your opponent's) have no Weakness.

text.flavor: When it sees a person, it digs a hole with its tail to make its escape. If you happen to find one, consider yourself lucky.

text.name: Stantler

attacks.name: Wild Dive
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage for each Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

text.flavor: The curved antlers subtly change the flow of air to create a strange space where reality is distorted.

text.name: Smeargle

attacks.name: Sketching Trash
attacks.text: Put up to 2 Fusion Strike Trainer cards from your discard pile into your hand.

text.flavor: It draws symbols with the fluid that oozes from the tip of its tail. Depending on the symbol, Smeargle fanatics will pay big money for them.

text.name: Skitty

attacks.name: Whimsy Tackle
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

text.flavor: It shows its cute side by chasing its own tail until it gets dizzy.

text.name: Delcatty

attacks.name: Willful Busybody
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand. Choose a card you find there and put it on the bottom of their deck.

attacks.name: Double Slap
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 50 damage for each heads.

text.flavor: It is highly popular among female Trainers for its sublime fur. It does not keep a nest.

text.name: Buneary

attacks.name: Double Kick
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 20 damage for each heads.

text.flavor: The reason it keeps one ear rolled up is so it can launch a swift counterattack if it's attacked by an enemy.

text.name: Lopunny
text.flavor: It's notably wary and has a dislike of fighting, but at the same time, it can deliver powerful kicks with its lithe legs.

text.name: Bunnelby

attacks.name: Find a Friend
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Pokémon, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Take Down
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 10 damage to itself.

text.flavor: It’s very sensitive to danger. The sound of Corviknight’s flapping will have Bunnelby digging a hole to hide underground in moments.

text.name: Diggersby

attacks.name: Take Down
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

text.flavor: The fur on its belly retains heat exceptionally well. People used to make heavy winter clothing from fur shed by this Pokémon.

text.name: Hawlucha

attacks.name: Flying Stomp
attacks.text: Discard a Special Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.
